chapters.screenText: Run your Python shelf script and save its native results.
chapters.screenWhy: Keep the source inputs, inspect native fields, and save a complete result package.
chapters.expectedResult: Have run.py, validate_dataset.py and icepack-shelf-small-v1.json ready.
chapters.title: Your goal: run your own Icepack script
instructions: Run a short Python shelf experiment, inspect its fields and save a complete results ZIP.
Have run.py, validate_dataset.py and icepack-shelf-small-v1.json ready.
chapters.note: Start with your approved cloud account connected and its resources prepared.
chapters.why: Keep the source inputs, inspect native fields, and save a complete result package.

chapters.screenText: Start here in CryoLauncher. Choose Cloud for this tutorial.
chapters.screenWhy: Your workspace keeps scripts, dataset references and results together.
chapters.expectedResult: Your workspace keeps scripts, datasets, run history and results together.
chapters.title: Start here
instructions: Open CryoLauncher and sign in. Use an approved connected cloud account with its resources prepared.
The following steps select this tutorial’s model and example.
chapters.note: Shared application orientation; the case-specific configuration follows.
chapters.why: Your workspace keeps scripts, dataset references and results together.

chapters.screenText: Choose Cloud → Advanced → Icepack.
chapters.screenWhy: Choose the intended interface, model and example before editing or launching a run.
chapters.expectedResult: Use a separate editable workspace for your script.
chapters.title: 1. Open an Advanced workspace
instructions: Choose Cloud → Advanced → Icepack.
You will keep this custom experiment in its own editable workspace.
chapters.note: This short 10 km shelf experiment is separate from the canonical spin-up example.
chapters.why: Choose the intended interface, model and example before editing or launching a run.

chapters.screenText: Enter a new name and choose New example.
chapters.screenWhy: An owned example stores your files separately from the supplied application source.
chapters.expectedResult: Create an owned workspace example for this experiment.
chapters.title: 2. Create your workspace example
instructions: Enter a new name, then choose New example.
chapters.note: You will create a separate editable workspace.
chapters.why: An owned example stores your files separately from the supplied application source.

chapters.screenText: Wait for the created-workspace message.
chapters.screenWhy: An owned example stores your files separately from the supplied application source.
chapters.expectedResult: This example is pilot-icepack-script-1118.
chapters.title: 2. Create your workspace example
instructions: Enter a new name and choose New example.
Wait for the created-workspace confirmation and empty file list.
chapters.note: This example is named pilot-icepack-script-1118.
chapters.why: An owned example stores your files separately from the supplied application source.

chapters.screenText: Choose run.py and validate_dataset.py in your file picker; Open.
chapters.screenWhy: Selecting local files prepares them for import; importing saves them in this example.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep the script and validator together.
chapters.title: 3. Select both Python files
instructions: Choose script files. In your file picker select run.py and validate_dataset.py, then choose Open.
chapters.note: Keep both Python files in the same example.
chapters.why: Selecting local files prepares them for import; importing saves them in this example.

chapters.screenText: Check the script picker changes from zero to two files.
chapters.screenWhy: Selecting local files prepares them for import; importing saves them in this example.
chapters.expectedResult: Selected files are not saved until you import them.
chapters.title: 3. Check the selected file count
instructions: The script picker changes from zero to two selected files.
You are ready to import the script and its validator.
chapters.note: Files are selected first; importing saves them.
chapters.why: Selecting local files prepares them for import; importing saves them in this example.

chapters.screenText: Choose Import script files.
chapters.screenWhy: Import saves the selected source files in this example; it does not launch the model.
chapters.expectedResult: Enable Replace existing script files if run.py already exists.
chapters.title: 4. Import the scripts
instructions: Choose Import script files.
chapters.note: If your example already contains run.py, enable Replace existing script files first.
chapters.why: Import saves the selected source files in this example; it does not launch the model.

chapters.screenText: Check Imported run.py, validate_dataset.py. Files are saved.
chapters.screenWhy: Import saves the selected source files in this example; it does not launch the model.
chapters.expectedResult: The file selector now contains the runnable script.
chapters.title: 4. Confirm both saved filenames
instructions: Wait for Imported run.py, validate_dataset.py. Files are saved.
The file selector now contains the runnable Python script.
chapters.note: Replace only the existing files you intend to update.
chapters.why: Import saves the selected source files in this example; it does not launch the model.

chapters.screenText: Set the Run target to run.py.
chapters.screenWhy: Run target selects the entry script; other imported files can act as helpers.
chapters.expectedResult: The validator checks the JSON before loading the scientific libraries.
chapters.title: 5. Use run.py as the entry point
instructions: Set Run target to run.py.
The validator checks JSON schema, model, units and bounds before the scientific libraries are imported.
chapters.note: Importing files does not launch a run.
chapters.why: Run target selects the entry script; other imported files can act as helpers.

chapters.screenText: In Datasets select icepack-shelf-small-v1.json.
chapters.screenWhy: Select the dataset that this script will reference and read at launch.
chapters.expectedResult: If it is absent, choose the data file and Upload it first.
chapters.title: 6. Select the JSON configuration
instructions: In Datasets select icepack-shelf-small-v1.json.
If it is not listed yet, add it with Choose data files → Upload first.
chapters.note: This workflow uses JSON configuration; gridded initial fields have their own tutorial.
chapters.why: Select the dataset that this script will reference and read at launch.

chapters.screenText: Choose Reference in example.
chapters.screenWhy: A reference stages this dataset under data/ when the selected example launches.
chapters.expectedResult: Use the supplied JSON filename as the reference alias.
chapters.title: 6. Reference it in your example
instructions: Choose Reference in example.
chapters.note: The script reads data/icepack-shelf-small-v1.json.
chapters.why: A reference stages this dataset under data/ when the selected example launches.

chapters.screenText: Confirm the reference saved in this example.
chapters.screenWhy: A reference stages this dataset under data/ when the selected example launches.
chapters.expectedResult: The script reads data/icepack-shelf-small-v1.json.
chapters.title: 6. Confirm the staged JSON path
instructions: Read the reference confirmation.
At launch, the JSON is copied to data/icepack-shelf-small-v1.json for the script to read.
chapters.note: The reference belongs to this workspace example.
chapters.why: A reference stages this dataset under data/ when the selected example launches.

chapters.screenText: Review the short 10 km × 10 km CG1 shelf experiment.
chapters.screenWhy: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.
chapters.expectedResult: One 0.01-year step; temperature 253.15 K; zero accumulation.
chapters.title: 7. Understand the short experiment
instructions: The domain is 10 km × 10 km with 4 × 4 subdivisions and CG1 thickness/velocity.
The script runs a diagnostic solve, one 0.01-year step, then another diagnostic solve.
chapters.note: Temperature is 253.15 K; accumulation is zero.
chapters.why: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.

chapters.screenText: Choose Review & Launch.
chapters.screenWhy: Review confirms the intended model, source, resources and charges before submission.
chapters.expectedResult: Check the owned example, run.py target and resources.
chapters.title: 8. Review the cloud configuration
instructions: Choose Review & Launch. Check the model, workspace example, run.py target and resources.
chapters.note: You should be reviewing the custom script example.
chapters.why: Review confirms the intended model, source, resources and charges before submission.

chapters.screenText: Control guide: confirm Launch cloud run when checks are Ready.
chapters.screenWhy: This confirmation stages the reviewed inputs and starts a paid cloud job.
chapters.expectedResult: The following card belongs to this tutorial’s original native run.
chapters.title: 8. Confirm the launch
instructions: Choose Launch cloud run when the readiness checks are ready.
This confirmation starts the run.
chapters.note: Control guide; the following card belongs to this tutorial’s original native run.
chapters.why: This confirmation stages the reviewed inputs and starts a paid cloud job.

chapters.screenText: Follow the new custom-script run card.
chapters.screenWhy: Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.
chapters.expectedResult: The native job used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB.
chapters.title: 8. Follow your queued run
instructions: The new run card names pilot-icepack-script-1118.
Allow it to finish, then open View results.
chapters.note: The native job used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB.
chapters.why: Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.

chapters.screenText: Open the completed native results.
chapters.screenWhy: A completed native job and its recorded provenance provide execution evidence.
chapters.expectedResult: Submission → start: 220.087 s; task: 48.192 s; script: 15.6633 s.
chapters.title: 9. Open the completed native results
instructions: The job completed successfully with exit code 0.
Open Results for this custom script run.
chapters.note: Submission → Batch start: 220.087 s; task: 48.192 s; script: 15.6633 s.
chapters.why: A completed native job and its recorded provenance provide execution evidence.

chapters.screenText: Select a field and use Render when needed.
chapters.screenWhy: The solution, field name, units and mesh counts identify what you are viewing.
chapters.expectedResult: The first field may preview automatically.
chapters.title: 10. Render a saved field
instructions: Results opens with an initial preview. Select a field and use Render when needed.
chapters.note: Use the displayed field name and units.
chapters.why: The solution, field name, units and mesh counts identify what you are viewing.

chapters.screenText: Inspect the native field summary.
chapters.screenWhy: The solution, field name, units and mesh counts identify what you are viewing.
chapters.expectedResult: 25 vertices / 32 triangles; finite CG1 thickness and velocity.
chapters.title: 10. Inspect the field view
instructions: This native export has 25 vertices and 32 triangles.
Thickness and velocity are finite CG1 fields; accumulation is zero.
chapters.note: Velocity is in metres/year; thickness is in metres.
chapters.why: The solution, field name, units and mesh counts identify what you are viewing.

chapters.screenText: Open the full saved thickness figure.
chapters.screenWhy: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.
chapters.expectedResult: Area-weighted mean thickness: 400.006923 m.
chapters.title: 11. Inspect the final thickness
instructions: Open the full saved thickness figure.
Thickness is 300.023425–499.981468 m, with area-weighted mean 400.006923 m.
chapters.note: Keep the original scientific PNG with your results.
chapters.why: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.

chapters.screenText: Inspect speed and direction in the saved figure.
chapters.screenWhy: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.
chapters.expectedResult: Domain RMS speed: 130.141951 m/year; arrows show direction.
chapters.title: 12. Inspect speed and direction
instructions: Colour shows speed and arrows show direction.
The domain RMS speed is 130.141951 m/year; independent field integration agrees with the script metric.
chapters.note: The figure is the unchanged downloaded archive member.
chapters.why: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.

chapters.screenText: Choose Download results.
chapters.screenWhy: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.
chapters.expectedResult: Wait for the fresh HTTPS archive link.
chapters.title: 13. Save your result archive
instructions: Choose Download results, then open the fresh HTTPS link.
chapters.note: Keep the ZIP with your script, validator and JSON.
chapters.why: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.

chapters.screenText: Open the new link and save the 11-member ZIP.
chapters.screenWhy: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep it with your script, validator and JSON.
chapters.title: 13. Keep the archive and inputs
instructions: Save the 11-member ZIP containing fields, mesh, figures, metrics and runtime/RNG provenance.
chapters.note: Use the current run’s generated link.
chapters.why: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.

chapters.screenText: Keep this short fixture’s scientific scope with the archive.
chapters.screenWhy: Keep the scientific input definitions and numerical qualifications with the result.
chapters.expectedResult: The 100→200 m/year initial guess is not an imposed outflow speed.
chapters.title: What this example establishes
instructions: The initial velocity guess rises from 100 to 200 m/year; 200 is not an imposed outflow speed.
This one-step fixture has no damage field or transient time axis. Its retained output checks are separate from an independent native repeat or accuracy assessment.
chapters.note: The supplied script, validator and JSON were bound to the accepted native run.
chapters.why: Keep the scientific input definitions and numerical qualifications with the result.
